'''''Andreaea rothii''''', or '''Roth's andreaea moss''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile?symbol=ANRO7|title=Plants Profile for Andreaea rothii (Roth's andreaea moss)|website=plants.usda.gov|access-date=2020-03-16}}</ref> is a species of [[moss]] in the family [[Andreaeaceae]] native to North America and parts of Europe.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eol.org/pages/855618/maps|title=Roth's andreaea moss maps - Encyclopedia of Life|website=eol.org|access-date=2020-03-16}}</ref><ref name=fna/> This plant was described in 1807 by Weber and Mohr.<ref name=fna/> 

== Description ==
''Andreaea rothii'' gametophytes sometimes form extensive black to brown cushion-like patches,<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Rothero|first=Gordon|title=Mosses and Liverworts of Britain and Ireland: A Field Guide|publisher=British Bryological Society|year=2010|isbn=978-0-9561310-1-0|editor-last=Atherton|editor-first=Ian|location=United Kingdom|pages=314|chapter=Andreaea rothii subsp. falcata / subsp. rothii|editor-last2=Bosanquet|editor-first2=Sam|editor-last3=Lawley|editor-first3=Mark}}</ref><ref name="fna" /> with individual shoots erect and less than 2 cm tall.<ref name=":1" /> The leaves of ''Andreaea rothii'' are 1-2 cm wide, and have a strong costa,<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200000843|title=Andreaea rothii in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2020-04-25}}</ref> which is roughly synonymous to a midrib. The leaves can be falcate-secund, curving to one side of the plant.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="fna" /><ref name=":0" /> This is especially true when wet, however the plants do not alter much when dry.<ref name=":1" /> The outline of the leaf is pear-shaped, swelling at the base and tapering to a tip,<ref name=":1" /><ref name="fna" /> and can also be strongly curved depending on subspecies.<ref name=":1" />   

== Distribution ==
''Andreaea rothii'' grows on rocks that are wet, acidic, and exposed.<ref name="fna" /><ref name=":1" /> This species is found anywhere from areas of high elevation to sea-level.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="fna" />

== Reproduction ==
''Andreae rothii'' gametophytes can be gonioautoicous—meaning the [[Antheridium|antheridia]] are bud-like in the axil of an [[Archegonium|archegonial]] branch—or cladautoicous—meaning the antheridia and archegonia are found on different branches of the same plant.<ref name=":0" /> Like all of the Andreaeaceae, [[Sporangium|sporangia]] are elevated on a pseudopodium,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_moss_gk.pl?genus=Andreaea|title=California Moss eFlora key to Andreaea|website=ucjeps.berkeley.edu|access-date=2020-03-16}}</ref> a structure resembling a seta but composed of gametophyte tissue rather than sporophyte tissue. The sporangia will dehisce longitudinally, forming slits through which spores are dispersed.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=10040|title=Andreaeaceae|last=|first=|date=|website=eFlora of North America|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071101051805/http://www.efloras.org:80/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=10040 |archive-date=2007-11-01 |access-date=}}</ref> This pattern of dehiscence gives the genus its common name: "Lantern mosses".
